data.gender_notes: Fintan is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish word 'Fionn' meaning fair or white and 'tan' meaning god. In Irish mythology, Fintan is a wise and powerful druid who survived a great flood. The name Fintan carries the meaning “Fair or White God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Fintan usually hope their child will grow to embody fair or white god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing divine wisdom and resilience.
data.etymology: Fintan belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair or White God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fintan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: In Irish mythology, Fintan is a venerated character known for his wisdom, magic, and survival against the odds. His name evokes images of ancient druidic practices and Celtic mythology. It is a popular name among Irish descendants and carries a rich cultural history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Fintan holds deep spiritual significance as it signifies 'God of the White' or 'White god'. The wise and powerful druid Fintan embodies the ideal of living in harmony with nature and fostering deep wisdom and knowledge.

It symbolizes the purity and valor of one who embodies both the spiritual and physical courage in the face of adversity. This name invites the bearer to strive towards inner light and outer strength, reflecting the enduring spirit of the Celtic sages.

historical_references.reference: According to Irish legend, Fintan was a mythical Irish hero and poet, also known as Fintan the Wise, who lived during the 4th and 5th centuries AD. He was a pupil of the famous Irish saint, St. Finnian of Clonard. Fintan was well known for his knowledge, wisdom, and poetic skills. One story tells of his encounter with a talking salmon, which he managed to outwit and eat, thus gaining the gift of prophecy. Another tale tells of his debate with St. Patrick about the nature of the Trinity, which Fintan won by explaining it in a poetic way that St. Patrick found convincing.

In early Christian hagiography, there is a Saint Finian of Lindisfarne, also known as Fintan, who lived during the 7th century AD. He was an Irish monk who is said to have founded the monastery on Lindisfarne, off the northeast coast of England. He was also a renowned teacher, and his students included St. Aidan, who went on to become the first Bishop of Lindisfarne and the Apostle of Northumberland. Fintan is said to have died on Iona, in the Inner Hebrides, in 615 AD.

modern_usage.modern_context: In Irish mythology, Fintan is a legendary figure known as the 'Salmon of Knowledge'. He is celebrated in various stories, particularly in the Ulster Cycle. In fantasy literature, Fintan is a popular character in Irish-inspired works such as 'The Dark and Bloody Ground' by Peadar O'Donnell and 'The Boldest' by Kevin Crossley-Holland. In modern times, Fintan is also known as a respected name in the cybersecurity industry. According to LinkedIn data, there are several professionals named Fintan who hold key positions in cybersecurity firms and organizations.
